evidence.estrutura: Sheikh was an educator and social reformer, not a constitutional theorist. Her work through local schools and household/community networks supports grassroots institution-building but does not establish a federal-versus-centralized state doctrine.
evidence.representacao: Her work deliberately expanded educational participation to girls, Dalits and other groups excluded from knowledge and public life. This supports inclusive social participation, though no formal electoral-system theory is documented.
evidence.poder: She persisted despite threats and opposition from dominant caste and religious conservatives and supported education as a means of emancipation. This supports resistance to coercive social hierarchy, but not a complete modern policing doctrine.
evidence.imigracao: No reliable immigration or border-policy position is established from the surviving historical record.
evidence.diplomacia: No developed foreign-policy or diplomacy doctrine is established.
evidence.intervencao: No developed military-intervention doctrine is established.
evidence.economia: Her educational mission targeted socially and economically marginalized groups and required collective/community provision, but no comprehensive ownership or redistribution doctrine survives.
evidence.controle: Her work supports public/community provision of education rather than laissez-faire neglect, but does not establish centralized economic planning.
evidence.comercio: No reliable trade-policy doctrine is established.
evidence.religiao: As a Muslim woman who collaborated across religious and caste lines and faced orthodox opposition, her work supports religious pluralism and reform rather than clerical control. A simple secular-versus-religious score should remain moderate.
evidence.moral: Girls' education, anti-caste work and willingness to defy restrictive gender norms strongly support progressive social values for her historical context.
evidence.tecnologia: Her work centered education and literacy in the nineteenth century; no meaningful modern technology-policy doctrine can be established.
